title: Retire the task time-budget from docs/MCP_SERVER.md, including a tool that no longer exists
description:
Filed by the governor on behalf of worker-de4739a8, who asked for this card at 12:21 while finishing task-0d11e05f and whose CLI died on the session limit before it could file. I verified every claim below against the tree rather than taking the request on trust.

THE DEFECT. The Wave 0 time-budget removal cleaned up the daemon schema, the JetBrains client and the VS Code client, and task-0d11e05f corrected docs/CONFIGURATION.md and docs/SCHEMA.md. docs/MCP_SERVER.md was never touched and still presents the feature as live.

The worst line is the one that documents a tool that does not exist:
- line 2105, `### moe.set_task_budget`, with a full contract at 2107 and a return shape at 2121: "Set or clear the wall-clock budget on a task. Daemon warns at 80% and escalates at 100% in #governors."
`grep budget packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/index.ts` returns nothing. CLAUDE.md is explicit that getTools() is the only registry and an unregistered tool is silently invisible to MCP. So an agent reading this doc will try to call a tool that is not there, and the failure will look like a daemon fault rather than a stale doc.

The rest describe removed behavior as current:
- line 258: `budget?: { wallClockMs?: number }  // soft cap on first-claim → DONE`
- line 273: the `budget.wallClockMs` validation rule and the preserved `warnedAt`/`escalatedAt` marks
- line 279: `budget` in the submit_plan return shape
- line 937: "After the claim, the daemon re-evaluates `task.budget` (warn at 80%, escalate at 100% to `#governors`)."

DO NOT SCRUB EVERY OCCURRENCE OF THE WORD. Three uses are live and unrelated, and deleting them is the likely failure mode of this task:
- lines 817 and 850: `maxDescriptionChars // summary preview budget`, a token budget
- line 943: "token-budgeted context"
- line 1990: "token-budgeted message window"
The reopen budget in schema.ts and the chat hop limit are also live, per the same warning task-0d11e05f recorded.

Docs-only. No source changes belong in this task.
definitionOfDone: docs/MCP_SERVER.md no longer documents moe.set_task_budget as an available tool; the section at line 2105 is removed, or explicitly marked removed if the file's conventions keep a tombstone for retired tools.

The live token-budget wording at lines 817, 850, 943 and 1990 is unchanged, verified by quoting those lines before and after.

Every remaining tool section in docs/MCP_SERVER.md names a tool that is actually registered in getTools(), verified by listing the doc's tool headings against the registry and reporting the comparison.
A guard test in the style of packages/moe-daemon/src/util/taskTimeBudgetDocs.test.ts (added by task-0d11e05f) covers docs/MCP_SERVER.md, fails on the current file, and passes after the edit.

GUARD EXTENDED IN PLACE (one home, as the plan required) — `packages/moe-daemon/src/util/taskTimeBudgetDocs.test.ts`. No second file. No production source touched. docs/MCP_SERVER.md NOT yet edited; that is step 3.

WHAT WAS ADDED
1. `DOCS.mcpServer` -> `<repoRoot>/docs/MCP_SERVER.md`. The three existing per-document assertions now run over it for free, including the deprecation one, so a surviving wall-clock mention must carry the sibling's marker rather than a new phrasing. `readDoc()` already throws a named-path error on a missing or empty file, and `repoRoot` already resolves from `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` — the error handling the step asked for was already right, so it was reused, not rewritten.
2. NEW `RETIRED_ANCHORS` entry `/budget\.wallClockMs/`. This is what catches line 273, which the existing anchors missed (`/^\s*(?:\*\s*)?budget\?:/` needs line-start). It is deliberately QUALIFIED: a bare `/wallClockMs/` would also match `TaskMetrics.wallClockMs`, which is LIVE — SCHEMA.md:729/738 document it as populated on `moe.qa_approve`. An unqualified anchor would have turned a live counter red. Comment in the file records why.
3. NEW describe `MCP_SERVER.md tool sections match the registry` — the generic form, not a hard-coded name. `TOOL_HEADING = /^#{2,6}\s+(moe\.[a-z_]+)\s*$/` extracts documented tool headings (the wider level range catches a retired tool demoted to another depth instead of deleted); `registeredToolNames()` CALLS `getTools(new StateManager({ projectPath: os.tmpdir() }))` and asserts the doc's headings are a subset. Runtime call, not source parsing — step 1 found `recordCandidate.ts` declares its name via a `TOOL_NAME` const, so any static parser would silently miss a tool and weaken the check. The StateManager is constructed, never `load()`ed: the constructor only joins paths, so nothing is written to os.tmpdir(). A companion case fails loudly if either the registry or the heading list comes back empty, so the subset check can never pass vacuously.
4. `LIVE_TERMS` gained the two MCP_SERVER.md token budgets with a new `minHits` field: `/summary preview budget/` minHits 2 and `/token-budgeted/` minHits 2. `minHits` exists because lines 860 and 893 are BYTE-IDENTICAL — a presence-only check would not notice one of the two being scrubbed. (i) No tombstone convention exists in this file (`grep -niE 'removed|retired|deprecat|tombstone'` finds only two unrelated prose hits), so DoD item 1's default applies.
